care_continuity: National isolation/CTE stock: 924, equal to the five provincial stocks (315 confirmed, 609 suspects).
Ituri: 407 patients (134 confirmed, 273 suspects) at a printed 40.0%, 34 critical; 88 admissions, 75 exits.

Nord-Kivu (page 7): 453 hospitalized (158 confirmed, 295 suspects), 330 in CTE/CT for 392 beds (printed 84.2%) and 123 in non-dedicated facilities; 330+123=453 reconciles. The 84.2% is a CTE/CT-only rate and the census exceeds the bed count, so no all-census occupancy is inferred. The care challenge prints the 123 as 29.9%, the SR152 share; 123/453 is 27.2%.
Haut-Uele: 43 patients for 169 beds (25.4%); one suspect critical at Pawa; 16 admissions and 18 exits.
Tshopo: 13 patients for 36 beds (36.1%), none severe; one suspect escaped the Meteo CTE and 3 confirmed cases remain lost to follow-up.
Bas-Uele: 6 suspects and 2 confirmed in isolation; 33 suspects remain in the community without adequate isolation.
challenges: Contacts 25956/33264 (78.0%) across six reporting provinces, down from 81.8% and below the 95% threshold; 7308 unseen (22.0%). Ituri is lowest at 74.4% (9394/12634); Nord-Kivu has 1727 contacts never seen, 1495 of them in Beni; Rungu zone (149 contacts) did not report; only Bas-Uele and Sud-Ubangi reach 95%. Sud-Kivu transmitted no data.

Alerts: 4048 reported and 3988 verified (98.5%), 612 validated (15.3%), all 612 investigated and 242 transferred (39.5%). 59 live alerts unverified (Haut-Uele 36, Tshopo 22, Bas-Uele 1); none of the Bas-Uele, Sud-Ubangi or Tshopo suspects transferred; Haut-Uele validates 3 deceased alerts of 2 received and Ituri verifies 83 of 85.

PoE/PoC completeness 111/119 (93.3%): Sud-Kivu 55.6% (5/9), Haut-Uele 90.0% with the Bombombi and Barriere Cadenas PoCs not reporting; Butuhe PoC (Nord-Kivu) non-functional since 26 September and Avakubi PoC (Ituri) non-functional for insecurity; Ituri PoC alerts under-encoded in DHIS2 Tracker with weak supervision mobility at Rwampara, Nizi and Bunia; Nord-Kivu PoC alerts not handled on time; Bas-Uele 19/41 sites functional (46.3%).

Ituri rings 20/36 (55.6%) with weak ECUMER coverage, too few teams at Mangala and Mandima, transport gaps in six zones and a provider strike over non-payment at Bunia; Haut-Uele only 5/7 zones sent IPC data; Bas-Uele 16/20 priority facilities without functional triage and 17/20 without 72-hour water storage; Nord-Kivu 50 EDS awaiting family consent and 27 of 49 deaths (55.1%) in non-dedicated facilities.

Ituri: 407 patients (134 confirmed, 273 suspects) at a printed 40.0% occupancy with no bed denominator, 34 critical; limited capacity at Mambasa, Kilo, Lolwa, Mangala and Biakato, no food for 10 patients in Mandima, ambulance movement reporting 21/33.
Nord-Kivu: CTE/CT occupancy 330/392 (84.2%), suspect beds 164/165 (99.4%) and 123 patients hospitalized outside CTE/CT (printed 29.9%, which is 27.2% of the 453 census).

Nord-Kivu ambulance response capacity limited to 50% (14/28) with incomplete ambulance data at Kalunguta, although all 19 runs of the day were completed; Bas-Uele has no ambulance for transfers and its standard CTE at HGR Buta is still under construction.

Haut-Uele: 43 patients for 169 beds (25.4%), weak network, staff demotivation, nutrition, water and electricity gaps; Tshopo: 13 patients for 36 beds (36.1%), lacking resuscitation equipment and PEP staff, with 3 confirmed cases lost to follow-up.
Tshopo: one suspect escaped the Meteo CTE (negative result) and 3 confirmed cases remain lost to follow-up. Bas-Uele: 33 suspects remain in the community without adequate isolation, 27 of them new.

Bas-Uele Ervebo stock out (0 doses) with coverage 11.4% (1500/13202); Ituri's target for frontline workers remains to be redefined (the challenge prints 1007 vaccinated against a provisional 1000, while the actions report a cumulative 1033). Vaccine logistics do not establish efficacy against Bundibugyo.

A baseline assessment of the CM de Nyakunde (listed under Nord-Kivu) found no triage circuit, no PPE, poor waste management, low blood product availability, under-equipped emergencies and substandard neonatology; 30/76 staff (39.5%) trained in IPC and 2 staff infected.

Ituri psychosocial coverage reaches 14/28 affected zones (50.0%) and Mandima is not covered; Bas-Uele SMSPS coverage is embryonic; Haut-Uele psychosocial agents lack mobility at Wamba and Boma Mangbetu; Tshopo needs trained agents at Wanie-Rukula.

Deceased alerts do not close: Haut-Uele validates 3 deceased alerts from 2 received, and Ituri verifies 83 of its 85. Printed 15.3% validated is 612/3988, over verified alerts. Sud-Kivu transmitted no data. Not repaired.

The same box says contact follow-up fell from 81.8% to 78.0% (correct) but remains 'above' the 95% threshold; the surveillance prose says below. Neither box is repaired.

Contacts: 78.0% is 25956/33264 across six reporting provinces; Sud-Kivu transmitted no data and Rungu zone (149 contacts) did not report within Haut-Uele. Nord-Kivu has 1727 contacts never seen, 1495 of them in Beni.

Nord-Kivu (page 7): 453 hospitalized (158 confirmed, 295 suspects), 330 in CTE/CT for 392 beds (printed 84.2%) and 123 in non-dedicated facilities; 330+123=453 reconciles. The 84.2% is a CTE/CT-only rate and the census exceeds the bed count, so no all-census occupancy is inferred. The care challenge prints the 123 as 29.9%, the SR152 share; 123/453 is 27.2%.

Ituri (pages 6-7) prints 407 patients at 40.0% occupancy (53.0% suspects, 25.0% confirmed) with no bed denominator; none is carried or back-calculated. All 88 admissions are suspects although Tableau 2 adds 31 Ituri confirmations. No cumulative Ituri recovery count is printed this edition.

Haut-Uele care panel (page 7): it reports 3 confirmed deaths (Isiro, Boma Mangbetu and Rungu); Tableau 2 has 2 (Rungu intra-CTE, Wamba community). It admits 7 confirmed cases, 5 of them at Wamba, while Tableau 2 gives Haut-Uele 5 new confirmations, 4 at Wamba. Not repaired.
Tshopo care panel (page 7): 2 deaths, 1 confirmed at the CTE and 1 suspect at Bafwasende; Tableau 2 prints 2 confirmed intra-CTE deaths at Makiso-Kisangani. Not repaired.

Isolation: the cover 924 equals the five provincial stocks 407+453+43+13+8, which split 315 confirmed and 609 suspects; no national split is printed. Haut-Uele (45+16-18=43) follows from SR152 plus same-day flows; Ituri 363+88-75=376 vs 407, Nord-Kivu 468+74-88=454 vs 453 and Tshopo 16+4-5=15 vs 13 do not. Bas-Uele lists 6 suspects and 2 confirmed (SR152: 11 suspects only) with no admissions; its 17 non-cases are not stated as isolation exits. Not repaired.

PoE/PoC (page 5): Tableau 4 covers Ituri, Nord-Kivu, Sud-Kivu, Tshopo and Haut-Uele (2 alerts, both Nord-Kivu bodies, 0 validated live suspects) and the prose agrees. The two bodies at PoC Foner Kasindi were referred for swabbing; no case is inferred. Ituri's 67th PoE/PoC positive was signalled on 11 October at Biakato Mayi (Mandima).

Laboratory (page 6): 506 samples, 65 positive (12.8%), split 41 living and 24 deceased. Tableau 2 has 22 community deaths: Nord-Kivu 10 and Haut-Uele 1 match, but Ituri has 13 deceased positives against 11 community deaths. Not repaired.
SMSPS challenge (page 9) says Mandima concentrates 32% of the day's notified cases; Tableau 2 gives Mandima 8 of 65 (12.3%). The sentence repeats SR151's text. Not repaired.

Vaccination (page 7): Ituri actions report 26 vaccinated on 13 October for a cumulative 1033; the challenge still prints 1007 vaccinated against a provisional target of 1000. Haut-Uele 470 of 1060 pre-registered (44.3%). Not repaired.
Cover (page 1): the text layer carries white-on-white '246 Aires de sante touchees Sur 3104 (7,9%)' that does not render; no health-area footprint is promoted.

Figure 1 is an onset-date plot of 7388 confirmed cases with onset date and vital status (SR152: 7284), not a cumulative count; bar heights are not reconstructed. Figure 2 maps are not a statistical source.
Continuity of care (page 8) lists a baseline assessment of the CM de Nyakunde under Nord-Kivu; it is recorded as printed and adds no zone.

Tshopo care bullet: 484 people have received experimental treatment since the start (41 confirmed, 443 post-exposure prophylaxis); the geographic scope is not stated. Ituri reports continued research on Ervebo efficacy against BDBV. Neither is an efficacy signal.
